extracted.intended_audience: covered entities and recipients of HHS Federal financial assistance (health programs and activities), health insurance issuers, group health plans, health care providers, compliance officers, and counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance and final rule preamble describing applicability, effective dates, phased applicability, and compliance obligations under HHS's Section 1557 nondiscrimination rule. Includes deadlines for procedural obligations, scope of coverage, treatment of subcontractors, plan benefit-design applicability, and exemptions/limitations (religious, tribal, conscience).

rubrics_metrics.name: General effective date for core discrimination prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining the overall 60-day effective date related to the general prohibition on discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, and disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 60-day effective date is consistent with prior rulemakings and applies to the general nondiscrimination prohibition; other provisions may have delayed applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased-in applicability for procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR is adopting phased-in applicability dates for certain provisions to allow covered entities time to designate a Section 1557 Coordinator and designee(s), develop and tailor policies and procedures, train staff, and develop required notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phased applicability provides additional time for implementation of organizational procedures and staff training; a chart of specific dates is provided in §92.1(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: No safe harbor for prior compliance with 2016 Rule notice/tagline requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to grant temporary safe harbors for covered entities operating under the 2016 Rule's notice and tagline language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR reasons that withholding enforcement would fail to recognize the importance of the new requirement; however, Notice of Availability requirements (auxiliary aids and services) have a delayed applicability date of one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed applicability for provisions requiring changes to health insurance or plan benefit design
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions that require changes to health insurance coverage or other health-related coverage, including group health plan benefit design for coverage newly subject to §92.207, have a delayed applicability date of the first day of the first plan year (or policy year in individual market) beginning on or after January 1, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This delayed date applies equally to calendar-year and non-calendar-year plans and gives issuers/plans time to implement plan design changes; example provided: a plan effective July 1, 2024 has until July 1, 2025 to comply if newly covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2020 Rule remains in effect until this final rule's effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2020 Rule remains in effect in the interim; covered entities subject to the 2020 Rule must continue to comply with the parts of the 2020 Rule that remain in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will interpret and enforce section 1557 under the 2020 Rule for coverages already subject to that rule, including prohibitions on discriminatory benefit design under §92.207(b)(1)-(5) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement approach for benefit-design complaints before Jan 1, 2025
rubrics_metrics.description: For complaints received prior to January 1, 2025 alleging discrimination related to benefit design, OCR will examine whether the coverage was subject to the 2020 Rule; if so, the covered entity is responsible for complying with §92.207(b)(1)-(5) as of July 5, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will consider the nature of the challenged feature and whether it would have been prohibited under the 2020 Rule; alleged integration-related discrimination will not be investigated under the final rule until after the delayed applicability date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered entities must comply with other provisions by their general effective dates even if benefit-design applicability is delayed
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities offering coverage subject to the delayed applicability date for benefit design are still required to comply with all other provisions of the final rule as of the general effective dates and specific applicability dates set forth in §92.1(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delayed benefit-design applicability is limited to benefit-design provisions; other duties (e.g., notices, policies) remain on their scheduled timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to health programs or activities receiving HHS Federal financial assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation applies to: (1) every health program or activity, any part of which receives Federal financial assistance, directly or indirectly, from the Department; (2) every health program or activity administered by the Department; and (3) every health program or activity administered by a title I entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reinstates a scope consistent with the 2016 Rule and is intended to ensure broad application of section 1557 protections to programs like Medicaid, Medicare, Exchanges, and other commercial plans receiving any HHS financial assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for employers and plan sponsors regarding employment practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation does not apply to any employer or other plan sponsor of a group health plan, including boards of trustees, associations, or other groups, with regard to employment practices, including the provision of employee health benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revision is intended to avoid duplication with employment nondiscrimination statutes and the agencies that enforce them; group health plans and employers remain separate entities requiring fact-specific analysis for coverage status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of provisions (§92.2(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If any provision of the part is held invalid or unenforceable by its terms or as applied to any person or circumstance, it shall be severable and not affect the remainder of the part or other persons/circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR gives examples (e.g., if Notice of Availability or Coordinator provisions were invalidated, other provisions would remain enforceable) and explains the provision allows the rule to function sensibly absent a struck provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary recipients and subrecipients are covered and independently responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: Both primary (direct) recipients and subrecipients (indirect recipients) of Federal financial assistance are covered by section 1557 and must comply independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under civil rights principles, both types of recipients are responsible; distribution of funds to subrecipients does not absolve the direct recipient of obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered entities remain responsible for subcontractors and cannot contract away civil rights obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A direct recipient may not absolve itself of its obligations by contracting with another entity to provide services for which it received Federal financial assistance; covered entities are responsible for the conduct of subcontractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors performing essential functions may themselves qualify as recipients; OCR cites case law (Frazier v. Board of Trustees) supporting that contractors carrying out core functions can be recipients under civil rights statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents and brokers treated based on fact-specific receipt of Federal assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether health insurance agents and brokers are subject to the rule depends on the contractual arrangement and whether they receive Federal financial assistance as a subrecipient; absent receipt, they are not subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents/brokers under contract with an Exchange could be covered as part of a title I entity's health program, but an independent broker assisting the public without receiving Federal funds generally is not covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of coverage already subject to the 2020 Rule (no delayed applicability for those benefit-design provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicare Advantage plans, Medicare Part D plans, Medicaid managed care plans, and qualified health plans are among examples of coverage subject to the 2020 Rule as of July 5, 2024 and thus subject to benefit-design provisions immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples illustrate categories of coverage that will be held to the benefit-design prohibitions without the Jan 1, 2025 delay because they were already covered under the 2020 Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective-date table for specific provisions (§92.1(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific compliance deadlines listed: §92.7 Coordinator within 120 days; §92.8 Policies and Procedures within one year; §92.9 Training following policies implementation and no later than one year; §92.10 Notice of nondiscrimination within 120 days; §92.11 Notice of availability within one year; §92.207(b)(1)-(5) and (b)(6) for newly covered plans by first day of plan year on/after Jan 1, 2025; §92.210(b),(c) decision support tools within 300 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table clarifies staggered timelines to permit operationalization; training must follow adoption of policies and cannot be later than one year from effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of Department coverage – limited to health programs/activities administered by HHS
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule applies to the Department's 'health' programs and activities rather than all Department programs and activities, reflecting the ACA's focus on health care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR may consider future rulemaking to expand scope, but for this rule it limits application to 'health' programs/activities to align with statutory purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation to HHS-funded recipients; other agencies retain enforcement for their funding
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule applies only to recipients of HHS funding; other Federal agencies have enforcement responsibility for health programs and activities they fund and administer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR's authority is limited to HHS-funded recipients consistent with its delegation to implement Section 1557 as applied to the Department and its recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious freedom and conscience protections and exemption process
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule recognizes that if application of any requirement would violate applicable Federal protections for religious freedom and conscience, such application shall not be required (§92.3(c)), and clarifies the exemption process at §92.302.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR proposes addressing religious objections through the exemption process rather than importing Title IX's religious exception; the rule clarifies process for exemptions and notes statutory conscience protections in the ACA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Indian Health Service (IHS) and tribal programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledges IHS and tribal programs are administered under a special government-to-government relationship; membership in federally recognized tribes is a political classification distinct from racial classifications, and exemptions (e.g., 45 CFR 80.3(d)) are adopted by reference in §92.101(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR intends to address any restrictions on application to IHS programs in the context of individual complaints and will apply statutory exemptions and defenses applicable under Federal law.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR will provide tools and resources to help determine covered entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR provides various tools on its website to help covered entities determine coverage status and will evaluate what further tools are helpful; points to the Department's TAGGS grants website to identify recipients of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical resources are available online to assist organizations in determining whether they are recipients of HHS funds and therefore covered by the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of litigation history and intent to reduce confusion
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR recognizes ongoing litigation and prior agency reversals have caused confusion and compliance burdens and states the final rule seeks to provide clarity and reduce burdens compared with prior rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR emphasizes efforts to answer questions and provide certainty about obligations; notes severability to limit impact of potential invalidations.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR administrative enforcement focus and private right of action
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule governs OCR's administrative enforcement of Section 1557; OCR reiterates that Section 1557 authorizes a private right of action but the rule's text pertains to OCR's administrative processes and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR notes employment disputes may be better addressed by other agencies, but private lawsuits under Section 1557 remain possible.
